blocks.text: **PowerPoint** builds a presentation as a sequence of **slides**. A slide is simply one page of the presentation. Each slide can mix text, tables, pictures, charts, shapes, SmartArt, audio, video, animations and transitions. PowerPoint is **proprietary** software owned by Microsoft.

blocks.title: Where it came from
items: Created at **Forethought, Inc.** by **Robert Gaskins** and **Dennis Austin** (principal creators); the original working name was **Presenter**

blocks.title: Open source
blocks.text: LibreOffice and Apache OpenOffice are two separate office suites, but both call their presentation program **Impress**, and it is free and open source. PowerPoint is not.

blocks.title: From a whole deck down to one box
items: Arrangement of placeholders on a slide

blocks.title: Words you must know
rows: A reusable starting file that holds design, layouts and sometimes sample content.
A coordinated set of colours, fonts, effects and backgrounds.
The arrangement of placeholders on a slide.
A preformatted container for text, pictures, charts, tables or video, often drawn with a dotted boundary.

blocks.title: A brand-new blank presentation
items: It normally opens with one **Title Slide**.
That layout has **two placeholders**: title and subtitle.
Placeholder count depends on the layout; the **Blank** layout can have none.
The usual unsaved file name is **Presentation1** (the number may increase for more new files).

blocks.title: Template vs Theme
blocks.text: A **template** supplies reusable structure (a whole starter file), while a **theme** only coordinates the look: colours, fonts, effects and backgrounds.

blocks.title: Parts of the PowerPoint window
rows: Shows the presentation name and application information; holds Minimise, Maximise/Restore and Close.
Frequently used commands such as Save and Undo.
Commands organised into tabs and groups. Modern PowerPoint uses a Ribbon; Menu Bar is older terminology.
Opens Backstage View for file management. PowerPoint 2007 used the Office Button instead.
Small slide previews, normally on the left.
Speaker notes for the current slide.
Bottom bar with view and zoom controls.
Navigate content; the thumbnail pane is not a scroll bar.

blocks.title: Open PowerPoint through Run
items: Press **Enter**. The program file is **POWERPNT.EXE**, and desktop PowerPoint must be installed.

blocks.title: File extensions
rows: PowerPoint Show; normally launches straight into Slide Show

blocks.title: Content you can place on slides
rows: Still or animated images; the animation normally plays during a slide show.

blocks.title: Extension memory trick
blocks.text: **x** = XML-based modern file. Then the letter before tells the job: **pptx** presentation, **potx** template (o for original), **ppsx** show, **pptm** macros (m for macro).

blocks.title: Presentation views
rows: Main editing view: thumbnails on the left, current slide in the centre, speaker notes below. It is the usual desktop default, though preferences can change it.
Shows titles and main placeholder text; good for structure and text editing. Pictures and manually inserted text boxes do not appear here.
Shows all slide thumbnails together to organise, rearrange or delete slides; large decks may need scrolling.
Edit a slide together with its speaker notes and prepare notes pages.
Review the presentation within a window.

blocks.title: Master views
rows: Holds the shared slide design, fonts, colours, backgrounds and placeholder positions. Use View -> Slide Master for consistent title formatting.
Controls how printed handouts look: header, footer, date, page number, orientation and arrangement.
Controls the shared look of printed notes pages.

blocks.title: Delivery views
rows: What the audience sees, normally full screen.
Speaker notes, slide previews, a timer and controls for you, while the audience sees only the presentation.

blocks.text: On the View tab there are **eight view commands**: five Presentation Views plus three Master Views. Add Slide Show and Presenter View and you reach the **ten** modes in this teaching list. That is a counting convention, not a rule that only Microsoft 365 has ten. The rest of the View tab holds groups: Show (Ruler, Gridlines, Guides, Notes), Zoom (magnification, Fit to Window), Color/Grayscale (colour, grayscale or black-and-white preview), Window (manage presentation windows) and Macros (automation, where supported).

blocks.title: Match the need to the view
blocks.text: Thumbnails of all slides = **Slide Sorter**. Text outline = **Outline**. Shared design for every slide = **Slide Master**. Printed handouts = **Handout Master**.

blocks.title: Master changes
blocks.text: Edits in Slide Master flow to the layouts and slides linked to it, but slides with direct formatting, or slides using a different master, may still need manual adjustment.

blocks.title: Layouts and placeholders
items: **Title Slide** is the usual first layout of a standard blank presentation, with two placeholders (title and subtitle).
A layout controls where content sits and how it is formatted.
A **placeholder** is a preformatted content container; it is not the same as an ordinary inserted text box.
Placeholder counts vary by layout, and a Blank layout can contain none.

blocks.title: Numbers worth remembering
rows: **10% to 400%**; zoom only changes on-screen magnification, not the real slide size
**1 pt to 3600 pt**, in 0.1-point steps (e.g. 10.3 pt, 105.7 pt)

blocks.title: Font and zoom traps
blocks.text: The dropdown's 8-96 pt is only a list of presets; type a size directly to go beyond it. The true maximum is **3600 pt**, not 4000. The 8-96 range is not a special limit for table text. Also, 100% zoom is selectable but is not a universal opening default: PowerPoint may fit the slide to the window or keep a saved setting.

blocks.title: Change the slide size
items: Pick **Standard**, **Widescreen** or **Custom Slide Size**. Existing files, templates or customised defaults may differ from the standard default.

blocks.title: Resize and special objects
items: To resize a picture, shape or text box: select it, then drag the sizing handles or type Height and Width under Picture Format / Shape Format.
An **Organization Chart** shows reporting relationships and employee hierarchy. Insert it with Insert -> SmartArt -> Hierarchy -> Organization Chart.
An organisation chart is a **SmartArt layout**, not a standard slide layout.
There is no universal maximum number of slides (50, 75 or 100 are not rules); a sensible length depends on purpose and time, and real capacity depends on resources, file size and performance.

blocks.title: File tab (Backstage View)
rows: Create a blank presentation or use a template.
Save with a different name, location or format.
Earlier versions, where supported (depends on storage and versioning).
Create PDF, video and other outputs.
Account and product details; send feedback; application settings.

blocks.title: Home tab groups
rows: Cut, Copy, Paste and Format Painter.
New Slide, Layout, Reset and Sections.
Typeface, size, colour and character formatting.

blocks.title: Insert tab groups
rows: Shapes, icons, SmartArt, charts and supported 3D models.
Hyperlinks, actions and supported Zoom links.
Text box, WordArt, header/footer, date/time, slide number and object.

blocks.title: Easy-to-mix pairs
blocks.text: **Ctrl + N** creates a new presentation, but **Ctrl + M** inserts a new slide. Chart is on **Insert**, Themes are on **Design**, Notes Page is on **View**. The File-menu Home page is a Backstage command, whereas the Ribbon Home tab holds the editing tools. Command availability varies by edition.
File = manage | Home = edit | Insert = add content.

blocks.title: Draw tab (ink)
rows: Pen type, ink colour and thickness.
Drawing aids such as a ruler.
Ink to Shape and Ink to Math, where supported.

blocks.title: Design tab
rows: Alternative colours, fonts, effects and backgrounds.

blocks.title: Review tab
rows: Finds barriers for users with disabilities.
Research/lookup tools in older interfaces that include them.
Compare/merge presentations in supporting older editions.

blocks.text: The ribbon tabs shown in the teaching picture are File, Home, Insert, Draw, Design, Transitions, Animations, Slide Show, Record, Review, View and Help (twelve). That count is not universal: tabs vary by version, platform, settings and selection. **Contextual tabs** such as Picture Format, Shape Format, Chart Design or Table Layout appear only when the matching object is selected. The pictured Ribbon is an older one: Compare and Merge was retired from Microsoft 365 PowerPoint for Windows from version 2502, and older research tools may be absent today. Handwriting and ink conversion depend on version, platform and device.
Draw = ink | Design = appearance | Review = check | Help = guidance.
A **transition** is the effect you see when the show moves from one slide to the next. It is applied to the entrance of the selected slide.

blocks.title: Transitions tab controls
rows: The gallery where you choose a transition.
Adjusts supported variations or direction (tied to the gallery, not always a separate group).

blocks.title: Gallery categories and examples
rows: Cut, Fade, Push, Wipe, Split, Reveal, Random Bars, Shape, Uncover, Cover, Flash

Fall Over, Drape, Curtains, Wind, Prestige, Fracture, Crush, Peel Off, Page Curl, Airplane, Origami, Dissolve, Checkerboard, Blinds, Clock, Ripple, Honeycomb, Glitter, Vortex, Shred, Switch, Flip, Gallery, Cube, Doors, Box, Comb, Zoom, Random
Pan, Ferris Wheel, Conveyor, Rotate, Window, Orbit, Fly Through

blocks.title: Timing settings
rows: Advance automatically after a set interval.
Use the chosen settings across the whole presentation.

blocks.title: Transition vs Animation
blocks.text: A **transition** changes **between slides**. An **animation** acts on text or another **object inside a slide**. None under transitions means no transition. Which effects exist, and how they are grouped, varies by version.

**Animation** controls how text, pictures, shapes and other objects on a slide appear, draw attention, move or disappear. The Animations tab has four areas: Preview, Animation, Advanced Animation and Timing.

blocks.title: Four principal categories
rows: Moves an object along a chosen route

blocks.title: Examples shown in each category
rows: Appear, Fade, Fly In, Float In, Split, Wipe, Shape, Wheel, Random Bars, Grow & Turn, Zoom, Swivel, Bounce.

Pulse, Color Pulse, Teeter, Spin, Grow/Shrink, Desaturate, Darken, Lighten, Transparency, Object Color, Complementary Color, Line Color, Fill Color, Brush Color, Font Color, Underline, Bold Flash, Bold Reveal, Wave.
Disappear, Fade, Fly Out, Float Out, Split, Wipe, Shape.
Preset lines, curves or other routes, or draw a custom path.

blocks.title: Advanced Animation
rows: Adds another effect without replacing the existing one.
Lists, inspects, reorders and manages effects; normally opens on the right.
Starts an effect after a specified action.
Copies animation settings from one object to another.

blocks.title: Timing
rows: On Click, With Previous or After Previous.
Waiting interval before the effect begins.

blocks.title: None is not a category
blocks.text: **None** simply means no animation. It is not a fifth category; the four are Entrance, Emphasis, Exit and Motion Paths.

blocks.title: Slide Show tab
rows: From Beginning, From Current Slide and Custom Slide Show.
Configure the show, hide slides, rehearse timings and manage playback.
Select the display and use Presenter View.
Present a chosen subset or sequence of slides from a larger presentation.

blocks.title: Rehearse Timings
items: Practise your talk while PowerPoint records the time spent on each slide.
Advance at the pace you intend to use.
Save the timings when prompted. Saved timings can then control automatic advancement.

blocks.text: Rehearse Timings measures delivery time only. To show a date or time on slides, use **Insert -> Date & Time**.

blocks.title: Record tab groups
rows: Save as Show and Export to Video.

blocks.text: Recording can capture narration and timings, and supported versions also record presenter video.

blocks.title: Controls during the show
rows: End the slide show (it does not advance)
Right Arrow, Down Arrow, Enter, Spacebar or N
Usually advances, depending on show settings
Return to the first slide during the show
Select the next / previous hyperlink or hotspot

blocks.title: Pen and practical notes
items: The presentation pen is **red** by default; other colours can be chosen. Draw-tab pens have their own settings.
An advance command may play the next animation before it changes slides.

blocks.text: F5 = beginning | Shift + F5 = current slide | Esc = finish | Rehearse = record timings.

blocks.title: Context matters
blocks.text: Ctrl + D also duplicates selected slide thumbnails, but **Ctrl + Shift + D** is the explicit slide-copy shortcut. Ctrl + Home goes to the first slide only depending on focus: inside a text box it goes to the start of that text, so during a show use **Home**. Shortcuts differ on Mac, mobile and the web.

blocks.title: Key pairs
blocks.text: Themes - Design and Notes Page - View are both correct pairs. Transitions change slides; animations affect objects.

revision: A slide is one page of a presentation; Apple's app is Keynote, Google's is Slides, and the open-source one is Impress.
Forethought created PowerPoint (Robert Gaskins, Dennis Austin; working name Presenter); Mac release and Microsoft takeover both in 1987.
A blank presentation opens with a Title Slide holding two placeholders (title and subtitle); unsaved name is Presentation1.
.pptx = presentation, .ppt = old 97-2003, .pptm = macros, .ppsx = show, .potx = template, .pps = old show.
Open PowerPoint via Run: Windows + R, type powerpnt (POWERPNT.EXE).
Views: Normal (default editing), Outline (titles and body text), Slide Sorter (thumbnails), Notes Page, Reading.
Masters: Slide Master (shared design), Handout Master (printed handouts), Notes Master (notes pages); all under the View tab.
Zoom runs 10%-400%; font presets 8-96 pt but the real range is 1-3600 pt; default ratio 16:9 since PowerPoint 2013 (4:3 before).
Themes and Slide Size are on Design; Spelling (F7) on Review; Chart, SmartArt and Org Chart on Insert.
Ctrl + N = new presentation; Ctrl + M = new slide; Ctrl + Shift + D duplicates a slide; Ctrl + D duplicates an object.
Transition = change between slides; animation = effect on an object inside a slide.
Four animation categories: Entrance, Emphasis, Exit, Motion Paths; Start options: On Click, With Previous, After Previous.
F5 starts the show from the beginning, Shift + F5 from the current slide, Esc ends it; the pen is red by default.
Rehearse Timings (Slide Show tab) records the time spent on each slide; Ctrl + K inserts a hyperlink; F12 is Save As.
